_notice: SYNTHETIC DEMONSTRATION DATA. Every symbol and agency below is invented. No real certification body, symbol, or trade dress is represented here.
_policy: verify_symbol identifies a symbol and nothing else. It returns no reliability field, no rating, and no acceptability judgement, by design — there is deliberately nothing in this data for an agent to leak on that question. See BRIEF 2d.

symbols.name: Kehilla-K
symbols.meaning: Certified pareve, or certified with no dairy or meat designation required.

symbols.mark: K in a rounded square followed by D
symbols.name: Kehilla-K-D
descriptors: k in a square with a d
k with a d next to it

symbols.mark: K in a rounded square followed by DE
symbols.name: Kehilla-K-DE
symbols.meaning: Certified dairy equipment — no dairy ingredients, produced on dairy equipment. Not the same as dairy, and not pareve.
descriptors: k in a square with de

symbols.mark: K in a rounded square followed by MEAT
symbols.name: Kehilla-K-Meat
descriptors: k in a square with meat

symbols.mark: K in a rounded square followed by P
symbols.name: Kehilla-K-P
symbols.meaning: Certified for Pesach for the year printed alongside. The P is a SEPARATE certification from year-round — its absence means the item is year-round only.
descriptors: k in a square with a p

symbols.name: VHM
symbols.meaning: A certification symbol belonging to another agency. We can identify it; we do not speak to another agency's standards.

symbols.mark: Interlocked B and D inside a triangle
symbols.name: BDT
symbols.meaning: A certification symbol belonging to another agency. Identification only.
descriptors: b and d in a triangle

symbols.mark: Script K with a small crown
symbols.name: KVR
symbols.meaning: A certification symbol belonging to another agency. Identification only.

symbols.mark: A bare letter K with no surrounding mark
symbols.name: Unqualified K
symbols.meaning: A bare K is not a certification symbol belonging to any agency we can identify. In the United States a plain letter K cannot be trademarked, so it does not identify a certifier. We cannot tell you who, if anyone, supervises a product bearing only a bare K — and what to do about that is a question for a Rav.
